articles.headline: The 2028 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Silly Season Shakes Up the Garage
articles.dek: Fresh faces and high-profile ladder moves headline the garage as the 2028 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series prepares to take the green flag.
articles.body:
The offseason garage shuffle is officially in the books, and the 2028 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series grid looks entirely overhauled before a single lap has been turned. Silly season delivered massive changes up and down the pit lane, setting up a fascinating dynamic for the year ahead.

Noah Gragson anchors the biggest veteran shift, dropping down to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series to pilot the Peterson Racing number 87 machine after departing Front Row Motorsports. Gragson brings instant Cup-level pedigree to the Peterson operation, immediately elevating expectations for the team as the new season looms.

Meanwhile, the ladder system continues to churn out top-tier talent. Layne Riggs steps up to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series to take over the Hendrick Motorsports number 17 ride, transitioning over from Front Row Motorsports. Joining him in the series influx is Gio Ruggiero, who makes the jump from Tricon Garage to wheel the JR Motorsports number 8 machine.

Upward mobility defined the rest of the major offseason moves. Sammy Smith departs JR Motorsports to move up to the Cup Series with Kaulig Racing in the number 16. Corey Day also makes the leap to the premier level, leaving Hendrick Motorsports to drive the number 4 for Front Row Motorsports. With the grid finalized, attention now turns to the season opener to see how these new manufacturer and team pairings perform under pressure.

posts.title: Corey Day to the 4 car in Cup
posts.text: Corey Day moving straight to the Front Row Motorsports 4 car is a massive reach and everyone pretending otherwise is nuts.
nah because his dirt stuff translates way better than people think. dude is gonna be fast right away
Dirt racing does not mean you know how to save tires on a two mile asphalt oval. We will see by race three.
My kid watches all the sprint car streams and swears Day is the next big thing. Time will tell if the asphalt transition is too steep.
he ate in the simulator tests though. FRM got a steal
Edit: fine whatever yall win we will check back in May
Who is making the biggest impact as a rookie in the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series this season?
layne riggs is about to dominate yall arent ready
gio ruggiero is locked in fr
nah rvg is mid wait till qualifying

posts.title: Gio Ruggiero jumping to JR Motorsports 8 car
posts.text: Ruggiero in the 8 car is the best move JRM made all offseason. Kid has raw speed.
Speed is fine but can he keep it off the fence during practice? Tricon equipment forgives a lot more than what JRM runs week to week.
He managed tires better than half the truck field last year. Just watch the long runs.
Fair enough. If he hits his marks on pit road he could snag an early win.
Exactly. Crew chief adjustments will be the main thing to watch.
Hearing whispers about Brett Poole's contract status beyond this year... keep an eye on the silly season board 👀
already putting together a parlay for who replaces him and its only preseason
is this confirmed or just another random rumor mill post
Just tracking the paddock chatter for now per multiple sources.
fair enough appreciate the clarity

posts.title: Sammy Smith to Kaulig 16 Cup car
posts.text: Sammy Smith getting that 16 Cup ride is wild. Kaulig better give him a decent chassis or he is gonna get chewed up.
Kaulig focuses heavily on fuel mileage tracks so if they can nail the strategy windows he will surprise some folks
fuel mileage strategy is just code for hoping everyone else wrecks so you finish fifteenth
That is literally how modern superspeedway and road course racing works whether you like it or not.
still a boring way to win
